title: Ancient Trees in Thailand: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Bodhi trees grown from Bodh Gaya cuttings, a king's warship ironwoods and a 53.5 metre yang na. {trees} trees across {places} places in Thailand.
intro: Most of the old trees we map in Thailand stand in temple grounds, and several arrived as cuttings of a holier tree. Bangkok alone has three bodhi trees with a recorded line. One at Wat Saket grew from saplings two monks carried home from Sri Lanka in 1814, one at Wat Phra Kaew from a shoot of the Bodh Gaya tree, planted in 1864, and one King Chulalongkorn nursed for nine years before planting it at Wat Benchamabophit in 1900. Others had harder jobs, ironwoods along a Bangkok canal grown as warship timber. Thailand's Ministry of Culture named Heritage Trees of the Land in lists from 2017 to 2019, and most trees here carry an entry, though its ages are often a temple's own account. The tallest we map is a yang na on Ko Pha Ngan, 53.5 metres by the register's measure.
